findings.failureScenario: On Windows, with no external editor configured, open_external runs `cmd /C start "" <path>` and passes the photo path as an ordinary argument. Rust's Windows argument quoting only wraps arguments that contain a space or tab, and cmd.exe does not follow the MSVC escaping rules, so its metacharacters (&, |, ^, %VAR%) stay live. The path comes from the library: Edit in External Editor (photo.editInExternal -> photo.editExternal result path) sends it through lc_native openExternalEditor. Importing and then editing a photo named like `IMG&calc&.jpg` (no spaces) makes cmd run `calc` as a separate command. Any legitimate filename with an unspaced `&` also fails to open the right file.
findings.action: Do not route file opening through cmd.exe. Use ShellExecuteW through a maintained opener crate (e.g. the opener/open crate or tauri-plugin-opener), or call `explorer.exe <path>` / `rundll32 url.dll,FileProtocolHandler`, so no shell parsing happens. If cmd must stay, validate the path and pass it with raw_arg using cmd-safe quoting and caret-escaping. Add a regression test with a path that contains `&` and `%`.
